text: Drink a big glass of water now. You just went a whole night without any.
Open the curtains or step outside. Daylight tells your body clock the day has started.
Make your bed. One task done before breakfast, and the room instantly looks calmer.
Keep your phone face down for the next 15 minutes. This morning is yours, not your feed's.
Get up at the same time every day, weekends too. Your body clock loves a routine.
Splash some cold water on your face. Cheap, fast and very effective.
Stretch for one minute: arms up, touch your toes, roll your shoulders. Wobble like me.
Tonight, put your phone across the room. Walking to it tomorrow is half the job.
Pick the one task that would make today a good day. Do that one first.
Eat something with protein this morning, like eggs, yoghurt or nuts. It keeps you full for longer.
Lay out tomorrow's clothes tonight. Fewer choices in the morning, fewer excuses.
Five minutes outside, even when it's cloudy. Outdoor light is far brighter than any lamp.
Take five slow breaths: in for four counts, out for six. Feel your shoulders drop.
Put on a song you love and play it loud. Dancing in the kitchen counts as exercise.
You skipped the snooze. Getting up straight away usually feels better than ten broken extra minutes.
Screens off half an hour before bed tonight. Tomorrow's wake-up will thank you.
Water first, coffee second. And try to keep coffee to the morning, so it doesn't steal tonight's sleep.
Think of three things you're looking forward to today. Small ones count.
Tidy one small thing: a cup, a shelf, a drawer. Tiny wins add up.
Send someone a good-morning message. Waking up is more fun when it's shared.
Count back seven to nine hours from your alarm. That's your bedtime tonight.
Smile at yourself in the mirror. It feels silly. Do it anyway.
Do the task you're dreading first. The rest of the day gets lighter.
Ten squats or a quick walk around the house gets your blood moving.
Don't open your email in bed. Out of bed first, inbox later.
A cool, dark bedroom helps you sleep deeper, so mornings get easier.
Get breakfast or your coffee ready the night before. Future you will be very grateful.
You already won once today: you got up. Keep that feeling going.
Write down today's plan in three lines. A clear head starts on paper.
End your shower with 30 seconds of cool water. Instant wake-up, no coffee needed.
Well begun is half done.
author: Aristotle

text: Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Lose an hour in the morning, and you will spend all day looking for it.
author: Richard Whately

text: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
author: Lao Tzu

text: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
author: Seneca

text: Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
author: Seneca

text: In the morning, when you rise unwillingly, let this thought be present: I am rising to the work of a human being.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
author: Marcus Aurelius

text: First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
author: Epictetus

text: Nothing is so fatiguing as the eternal hanging on of an uncompleted task.
author: William James

text: Dost thou love life? Then do not squander time, for that's the stuff life is made of.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Something attempted, something done, has earned a night's repose.
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow

text: The early bird catches the worm.
author: Old proverb

text: The morning hour has gold in its mouth.
author: Old proverb

text: Hope is a good breakfast, but it is a bad supper.
author: Francis Bacon

text: Think in the morning. Act in the noon. Eat in the evening. Sleep in the night.
author: William Blake

text: The sun himself is weak when he first rises, and gathers strength and courage as the day gets on.
author: Charles Dickens

text: The best way out is always through.
author: Robert Frost

text: One today is worth two tomorrows.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Well done is better than well said.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Life is either a daring adventure or nothing.
author: Helen Keller

text: Fortune favours the bold.
author: Virgil

text: Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: Write it on your heart that every day is the best day in the year.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
